title: How any change lands
question: When Claude changes something, what happens before it is on main?
summary: Every change, code or docs or design, goes through an independent review by a fresh agent before it is called done. Routine Git is the agents' job; a short list of irreversible things stays yours.
tldr: Each session starts from the `session-handoff` doc on `main` (`backlog/docs/`) and ends by rewriting it after a `Session Sweep`.

Build, prove it with `tests/run.py`, then a fresh reviewer per round: `code-reviewer` for code and everything not agent context; `design-reviewer` for looks. A `context-reviewer` reviews changes to agent rules.
Fix every Blocking and Material finding; stop at PASS or after 5 rounds (10 unattended). Then merge, push and watch CI.

status.title: The 2026-10-04 merges were reviewed after the fact
status.note: On 2026-10-04 you asked for every branch to be merged so only `main` remains; those merges had no review report. On 2026-10-14 a `context-reviewer` reviewed them (FINDINGS: ungated designs and open review reports brought onto `main`, stale records), and TASK-33 fixed each finding. Changes in flight are the Active and Review tasks in `backlog/`.

steps.title: The session starts from the handoff doc
steps.summary: Claude reads AGENTS.md, your preferences, then the `session-handoff` doc as it stands on `main`, and checks it against Git and the evidence.
does: Gives you a four-line briefing: Goal, Now, Next, You.
Separates an approved design from built behaviour, and old checks from current proof.
Runs `scripts/proposals.py` and tells you its one line: how many proposals wait on you, and how many are approved but not applied.

steps.title: A task file for the task
steps.summary: A Backlog.md task in `backlog/tasks/` is the task record: outcome, acceptance, plan, result and evidence, review, handoff. It changes on the branch doing the work.
does: Statuses: Queued → Active → Review → Ready → Done. The `blocked` label when stuck.
Ready is not Done: Done means on its branch, pushed, CI green, evidence recorded.

steps.title: A branch, or straight to main
steps.summary: Small verified fixes and docs may go straight to `main`. Features and anything uncertain get a `<type>/<topic>` branch, in a worktree under `.worktrees/`. No pull requests.

steps.title: Build it and prove it
steps.summary: Understand the seam first, then change it, then run ruff and the full suite. A visual change also needs a rendered page.
does: Evidence goes to a new `builds/tests-<timestamp>/` folder; nothing is overwritten.
Going around a component? It gets a `Framework Gap` entry before "done".

steps.title: Independent review
steps.summary: A fresh agent that never saw the work judges the exact snapshot. Which reviewer depends on what changed.
does: Code, tests, fixtures, and everything not agent context that no other gate covers: `code-reviewer`.
Looks: CV pages, brand assets, `Flagship` changes: `design-reviewer`.
Agent context (AGENTS.md, rules, glossary, skills): `context-reviewer`; a change that mixes code and context gets both.
Eight lenses, from product fit to repository hygiene. Findings are Blocking, Material, Minor or Note.

gate.label: Verdict PASS, FINDINGS or INCOMPLETE (never treated as PASS).

steps.note: Only spelling, comments, formatting or a glossary row skip the round, and record-keeping commits (storing reports, merging reviewed work).

steps.title: Fix Blocking and Material
steps.summary: Each report is kept word for word with the lead's dispositions beside it. Blocking and Material get fixed; the checks run again.

loop.label: A fresh reviewer, given every earlier report
loop.cap: At the cap the task stays unresolved and comes to you; more rounds need your decision.

does: Minor: fix it or record why it waits. Notes do not block.
Renaming the task never resets the round count.

steps.title: Merge, push, watch CI
steps.summary: Merging into `main` is routine and the agents' job. `main` must always be releasable.
does: Required checks before the push, then `gh run watch` until CI is green.
Then the task moves to Done with its evidence, as a record commit on `main`.
steps.note: Yours only, with the exact command shown first, including: deleting or force-pushing `main`, rewriting its published history, rewriting the private repo's history (the delete-by erase, which you run), `archive/*` tags, repo settings (public and private repo), deleting under `private/` or `.local/` or outside the repo, removing revisions, approvals, exports or portraits, replacing the `Release`.

steps.title: Session Sweep
steps.summary: Before stopping, Claude looks in fixed places for loose ends: a list of places to look, never a list of what is open.
does: Reviews: every commit on `main` since the handoff doc's `Main at` sha has a report or is trivial.
Proposals marked `approved` but not applied; tasks in Active, Review, Ready or labelled `blocked`.
Git leftovers, CI on `main`, old `builds/` folders.
Repo health: `/repo-maintenance quick`, a few seconds.
`Atlas`: `atlas.py check`; a stale or unverified page is re-checked against its sources.

steps.title: Rewrite the handoff doc on main
steps.summary: The next session starts here: written date, `Main at` sha, where things stand, next steps, your parked decisions, pitfalls.

steps.title: You get the report
steps.summary: A short verbal report and, for finished work, an HTML page. Decisions that need you are named.
steps.you: Read it, use the product, answer the parked decisions when you are ready.

gate.label: Product decisions and real-client approvals stay yours.
